about: The 11 criteria of the Policy Plus plan (plan.json built 2026-11-18) that audit E3 confirmed contradict the chosen journey. `to` is what the step makes the rule do, written from the step's `system` for this fixture: the journeys of that run had no `changes`.

cases.title: Find policies by the words you remember
cases.says: Given a phrase was opened with a double quote and never closed, when the search starts, then that phrase is left out and the search is wider than the person may expect.
cases.system: Searches title, description and comments of both areas by default, and shows results as words are given; says plainly when words are needed and when a quote was never closed.
cases.to: The search says plainly when a quote was never closed.

cases.title: Find policies by the words you remember
cases.says: Given the search text is empty, when the person starts the search, then no search runs and they are told "Please enter search terms."
cases.system: Searches title, description and comments of both areas by default, and shows results as words are given; says plainly when words are needed and when a quote was never closed.
cases.to: The search says plainly when words are needed, and results show as words are given.

cases.title: Find policies by the words you remember
cases.says: Given the person has unticked In title, In description and In comment, when they start the search, then no search runs and they see "At least one attribute must be searched. Check one of the boxes and try again."
cases.system: Limits the search to the chosen places and never allows none.
cases.to: The search is limited to the chosen places and never allows none.

cases.title: Find policies by the words you remember
cases.says: Given words and at least one place are chosen, when the person starts the search, then one search starts with what they entered, over both the user and the computer areas, comments included.
cases.system: Searches title, description and comments of both areas by default, and shows results as words are given; says plainly when words are needed and when a quote was never closed.
cases.to: Title, description and comments of both areas are searched by default and results show as words are given.

cases.title: Turn a typed user name into a valid account identifier
cases.says: Given a name typed in the user dialog, when the person presses Search, then it is turned into the account's SID; if it cannot be translated, they are told "The name could not be translated to a SID."
cases.system: Takes a name or a security identifier; a name is translated at once and the person is told when it cannot be; a valid identifier is accepted; an invalid one is refused with a message saying what to enter; leaving without choosing is always possible.
cases.to: A name is translated at once and the person is told when it cannot be.

cases.title: Turn a typed user name into a valid account identifier
cases.says: Given a name typed but no SID, when the person presses OK, then the name is looked up first and the dialog stays open if no SID results.
cases.system: Takes a name or a security identifier; a name is translated at once and the person is told when it cannot be; a valid identifier is accepted; an invalid one is refused with a message saying what to enter; leaving without choosing is always possible.
cases.to: A name is translated at once, with no separate search, and the person is told when it cannot be.

cases.title: Turn a typed user name into a valid account identifier
cases.says: Given a SID text, when the person presses OK, then it must be a valid SID or they are told "The SID is not valid. Enter a SID in the lower box, or enter a username in the top box and press Search to translate."; a valid SID is returned and the dialog closes.
cases.system: Takes a name or a security identifier; a name is translated at once and the person is told when it cannot be; a valid identifier is accepted; an invalid one is refused with a message saying what to enter; leaving without choosing is always possible.
cases.to: A valid identifier is accepted at once; an invalid one is refused with a message saying what to enter.

cases.title: Apply a checked semantic policy text to the policy sources
cases.says: Given several policies, when one fails, then it is skipped and counted and the rest are still applied; only the number of failures is known, not which policy or why.
cases.system: Offers apply only for a text that read correctly, then writes, skips and counts failures per policy and reports the outcome.
cases.to: Failures are skipped and counted per policy, and the outcome names each policy that failed.

cases.title: Open another user's stored settings file as a source
cases.says: Given the file cannot be opened after loading, when the source is used, then it silently becomes an empty read-only scratch source.
cases.system: Reopens the remembered user and computer sources, or the local Group Policy on first start; closes any sources already open, works out each source's location and whether it can be saved, and falls back to the defaults with a notice when the remembered ones cannot be reached.
cases.to: The workspace falls back to the defaults with a notice when a remembered source cannot be reached.

cases.title: Provide an empty scratch source and policy files on the machine
cases.says: Given the policy file of a POL file source, the local Group Policy or a per-user Group Policy does not exist, when the source is opened, then it is created empty with its folder and treated as writable, so a mistyped SID creates a new folder and empty file under the per-user policy folder; if creation fails, an empty read-only source is used and no error is shown.
cases.system: Reopens the remembered user and computer sources, or the local Group Policy on first start; closes any sources already open, works out each source's location and whether it can be saved, and falls back to the defaults with a notice when the remembered ones cannot be reached.
cases.to: The workspace falls back to the defaults with a notice when a remembered source cannot be reached.

cases.title: Open the policy dialog and finish it with OK, Apply or Cancel
cases.says: Given the person presses Cancel, when Apply was used earlier in the visit, then the dialog is reported as a change, and as a cancel otherwise; closing in any other way follows the same rule.
cases.system: The system applies the forecast, reports the outcome as a change if anything was saved in this visit, and keeps the person on the policy or closes it.
cases.to: One confirmation saves and leaves, and the outcome is reported as a change when anything was saved in this visit.
